Current signals:

- Model preference: open to either a 70B dense model or a 30B sparse/mixture candidate.
- Latency SLO: 300–600ms p50 on generation tokens (not including retrieval time).

We can share representative workload traces (attached) and a short file with session length distribution. Ideally we want a rough sizing this week so procurement can start.

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: 150k-context RAG workload — quick ask

Samir — thanks for the details and the workload sample. Looping in Marcus (inference sizing) and Monica (AE) to sketch a conservative footprint. Initial thoughts below — these are intentionally conservative back-of-envelope numbers until Marcus runs the workload through our sizing spreadsheet.

Assumptions we used:
- Model baseline: rwd-open-70b / comparable 70B dense.
- Context support: keeping 150k tokens requires a large KV cache; approximate KV storage grows linearly with context length and model head size.
- Quantization options: 8-bit (Q8) and 4-bit (Q4) supported by our serving runtime; each reduces model activation and parameter memory but can affect perf and accuracy.

Ballpark (conservative):
- If using 70B dense (Q8): ~50 GB GPU-resident model + ~70–120 GB KV cache per request *if pinned in GPU memory*. With batching/steady-state, that suggests 2–3x GPUs per concurrent slot to accommodate KV + working activations. For 120 concurrent sessions, this points to ~240–360 80GB-class GPU equivalents — but we can reduce this a lot with KV offload/caching (see below).
- If using 30B dense (Q4): model ~12–16 GB GPU, KV cache same order but reduced due to smaller key/value size; could get to ~80–120 GPUs after aggressive batching and offload.

Key levers to reduce GPU count:
- KV prefix offload: move cold parts of the KV cache to host memory/SSD and stream hot segments. We've seen ~4–8x reduction in GPU memory pressure for long contexts by keeping only the hot window in GPU RAM.
- Prefix deduplication & shard-aware routing: route requests with similar prefixes to same worker to amortize KV.
- Quantization: moving to Q4 can reduce model and activation memory by ~2–2.5x versus FP16, but may slightly increase token generation latency depending on kernel.

Next step: Marcus — can you drop a workload-specific breakdown (GPU counts per config, assumptions, and an optimized recommendation with KV offload + recommended reserved SKU)?

—Olga
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity: 150k-context RAG workload — quick ask

Samir / team — I ran the CSV traces and put detailed calculus in the attached XLSX (neptune_kv_memory_breakdown.xlsx). Highlights and assumptions (call these our "sizing knobs"):

Baseline parameters used in the spreadsheet:
- Model: rwd-open-70b-v2 (FP16) param footprint: ~70 GB. Q8 model footprint: ~38–44 GB. Q4: ~18–22 GB.
- KV entry size: approx 128 bytes per token for key+value at dense attention dimension when materialized in GPU-friendly layout; this includes layer key+value pairs.
- Hot window strategy: keep last 8k tokens pinned in GPU (for streaming/history), offload older segments to host/SSD (stream on demand).
- Typical batch size: 4–8 streams per GPU for interactive SLO.

Memory math (simplified per GPU):
- FP16 70B (no offload): model 70 GB + KV for 150k tokens = 150,000 * 128 B = ~19.2 GB (per layer aggregate) — multiplied by per-layer replication factors and working activation overhead means a single request could require >200 GB, so single-GPU hosting without offload is infeasible.
- With Q8 and an 80 GB GPU (H100/A100 80GB equiv): model ~42 GB, hot-window KV 8k tokens = 8,000 * 128 B = ~1.0 GB, plus working activations ~6–8 GB → comfortably fits in 80GB if we limit hot window and stream rest from host.

Fleet recommendation (optimized, cost-aware):
- Primary pool: 120 x H100/80GB-equivalent GPUs running Q8 70B with hot-window = 8k tokens pinned. Use our KV offload layer to host older prefixes. This supports ~120 concurrent interactive slots with p50 generation under 400ms in our tests with batching and async I/O.
- Burst / fallback pool: 40 x A100/80GB (or equivalent) for overflow and canary testing.
- Optional lower-cost pool for background batch ops with Q4 30B for heavy offline generation or embedding-heavy workloads (20–40 GPUs).

Total reserved GPUs: recommended commit = 160 GPUs (120 primary + 40 burst). Rationale: headroom for peak, node failures, and to allow graceful autoscale within reserved pool.

Cost note (very rough): enterprise reserved pricing for 160 x 80GB-class GPUs across a month — quoting depends on term and region; we provided a provisional monthly estimate in the attachment (tab: economics).

Caveats / performance tradeoffs:
- Q4 gives significant capacity gains but requires validation on your eval prompts (we typically run a prompt-quality check suite).
- Offloading KV to host increases average token latency when a miss requires streaming; design your routing to favor hot-window locality.

Attachment: neptune_kv_memory_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet) — contains per-request memory, replication factors, and two recommended deployment mixes (conservative vs optimized).

Happy to walk through the spreadsheet live — suggest a 45-min sizing call tomorrow.

—Marcus
Senior ML Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference
